title: Prime-field small-x factor bases: relation yield and cost (B11/A5)
question: Prime-field factor-base question (B11/A5 open requirement): for E/F_p (p prime) and the factor base V_B = {Q in E(F_p): x(Q) < B} with B = p^{1/m}, the probability that a uniformly random R in E(F_p) is a sum of m points of V_B is about |V_B|^m/(m! p) (heuristic), and finding such decompositions via Semaev summation polynomials (S_3 for m=2) costs at least as much as rho at toy sizes; no choice of (m, B) yields a relation-collection cost below sqrt(p) group operations on prime fields at toy sizes.
rationale: Highest-significance open direction for universal ECDLP identified independently by agents A (A5) and B (B11); cheap falsification at toy sizes.

next_action: Literature-verify Semaev 2004 / Petit-Kosters-Messeng 2016 prime-field results; consider non-small-x factor-base definitions (e.g. x in a multiplicative subgroup, or images of a small-degree map) as a falsifiable variant.
notes: Registered by PI. Known context (unverified recollection by agents): Semaev 2004; Petit-Kosters-Messeng PKC 2016; Diem; prime-field variants remain exponential. | ECDLP-12 (pre-registered, PI-reproduced): SURVIVES on tested domain (12 prime-order curves near 2^12..2^18, m in {2,3}, beta in {0.5,1,2}, exact enumeration). Best total cost 15.7 x sqrt(p) at 2^18 (falsification needed < 0.5 x). Measured pi tracks n^m/(m! r) within 0-30% (n counts signed points); the (2n)^m form in the statement double counts signs (statement imprecise). Semaev S_3 route verified (8000 group-law checks; 600/600 vs brute force) and ~2-2.7x cheaper than naive scanning but not cheaper than a full (m-1)-sum table (BSGS-like). Fitted exponents 0.6-1.0; agent derived m/(2m-1) > 1/2 inside its table cost model (not general). End-to-end toy index calculus recovered k correctly at p=4001, 15791 (40-52 x sqrt(p)).
